A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–I are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original OOD detection and transfer experiments with VGG, ResNet, and ViT models, including neural-collapse measurements and extensive ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original NECO comparisons, SGD experiments, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The encoder, frozen two-layer ETF projector, trainable classifier, entropy regularization, normalization components, and separate detection/transfer representations remain unchanged. SGD is an additional experimental variant, not a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-100, ImageNet-10 supplementary experiments, and the same eight OOD datasets: ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, Flowers, NINCO, CUB, Aircrafts, Pets, and STL-10. Audio, text, and regression appear only in v2's discussion.

E2.justification: v2 adds NECO as an external NC-based detection comparator across VGG17, ResNet18, ViT-T, and eight OOD datasets (Tables 5 and 22). This substantially expands comparison beyond v1's standard DNN baselines and component variants, which remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds SGD evaluation with learning rate 0.2, weight decay 0.0001, and batch size 512, plus runtime/FLOP profiling. Existing training and evaluation protocols remain. The ViT-Small caption changes 23.03M parameters to 21.62M, while Appendix A.1 retains 23.03M; an actual model-size change is unresolved.

E4.justification: The existing ablations and training-dynamics analyses are retained. v2 adds a focused optimizer-robustness check using SGD (Appendix H.6) and computational-efficiency measurements (H.8), supplementing the established experimental suite.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Dataset averages and the existing Pearson-correlation reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All matched original table results remain unchanged. v2 adds NECO average detection errors of 77.82/88.13/85.67 against the method's retained 65.10/69.70/83.16 for VGG17/ResNet18/ViT-T. New SGD results and compute overhead below 0.3% add substantial evidence (Tables 8, 20, and 23). Table 22 also reports individual datasets where NECO wins.

T1.justification: Appendix E replaces the proof sketch with a latent-class and entropy-chain-rule derivation, making the finite mixture-entropy bound explicit. The conclusion is unchanged. The expanded proof explicitly assumes component entropies diverge to minus infinity, although Proposition E.1 still states only weak convergence.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 2 narrows the theoretical contribution: v1 describes theory explaining both entropy regularization and ETF-induced collapse; v2 distinguishes entropy theory from empirical ETF evidence. The abstract and central detection–generalization trade-off claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of the vision/classification scope and possible audio, text, detection, and regression applications. Appendix H adds optimizer trade-off and scalability interpretations. These broaden applicability arguments without new evaluations outside the retained vision tasks.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/project link, SGD hyperparameters, and profiling details: four RTX A5000 GPUs for training and single-GPU DeepSpeed FLOP measurement. Expanded captions clarify retained experimental controls and embedding choices. The linked resource's availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds NECO, Ergen et al. (2022), and Pan and Cao (2023), and replaces the Mialon projector reference with Wang et al. (2022a). It also withdraws v1's claim that normalization's relationship to NC was unexplored, while retaining the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language edits, adds an experimental roadmap, expands the proof presentation, and inserts comparison and analysis subsections. The main narrative and Appendices A–I retain their established organization rather than undergoing extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds NECO, SGD, and compute tables, expands captions, and adjusts table highlighting and placement. All nine figure graphics and all original tables are retained; Figure 4 is relocated. The overall two-column presentation remains.

improvement.justification: The NECO comparison, SGD robustness check, cost measurements, and clearer experimental documentation improve empirical support and assessability. The narrowed theory contribution also helps. Gains remain limited: Appendix E retains a mismatch between its stated assumptions and proof, and Table 22's dataset-level exceptions qualify Section 6.5's new claim of superiority across 'all settings'.
